properties.name: Unbounded build iteration is noticed and surfaced — a HARD STOP is one option, not the requirement
properties.statement:
REASSESSED 2026-07-28, same day, on Anthony's instruction not to treat reflow's workflows as canon. First written as "the build loop is bounded, and exhausting the budget forces a return to the design", which took reflow's halt-and-resync as the requirement rather than as one candidate mechanism. The name now separates the two.

THE REAL GAP, which stands on its own: reflow2 MEASURES design erosion under repeated build rounds and never ACTS on it. The erosion trial asks the sharp question — after N rounds of test-fails/fix-code/accept, does the design still describe what it should — and is a regression gate, so the decay is known and quantified. Nothing ever interrupts. A session can iterate indefinitely and reflow2 will faithfully record the drift afterwards. That is a real hole, whatever the response turns out to be.

WHY THE HARD STOP IS DOUBTFUL AS THE ANSWER. reflow halted after three P3/P4 loops and forced a resync to architecture. Three objections. (1) It is PHASE-SHAPED: "go back to P2" presumes there is a P2 to go back to, and reflow2 has layers of a golden thread, not phases. (2) A hard stop is a poor fit for the operating context this project exists for — continual evolution against functional production code, where halting the work is rarely the right answer and is exactly the move that gets a discipline abandoned by the people it is meant to help. (3) Any fixed count is arbitrary. reflow at least ASKED for it (phases/P0_setup elicits the budget, default 3, range 1-10, alongside the mode and drift tolerance) which is better than compiling it in — but eliciting an arbitrary number does not make it meaningful, only chosen.

WHAT IS MORE LIKELY RIGHT, and it fits the discipline reflow2 already committed to. dec:report-dont-judge says report and ask rather than decide; the loop nudge and cap:read-loop-hint already surface debt when it is real without blocking anything. The natural shape here is the same: NOTICE that the build has been iterating without the design moving, and SAY SO with evidence — which is a computed observation, not a threshold. The evidence is already available: unresolved DriftEvents accumulating, a design_holds/design_updated history that confirm.rs can already read as dishonest (five holds with zero design edits), coverage moving the wrong way. Escalation, if any, belongs to req:drift-rolls-up-to-a-score, which was reassessed the same day for the same reason.

DISTINCT FROM cap:budget, which rolls a RESOURCE budget against a Constraint (mass, cost, power). Whatever is built here is about the design PROCESS, and reflow2 has no vocabulary for that.

Worth keeping from the review, because it answers the obvious objection that any of this is waterfall legacy: reflow's own P5_operations phase_definition states "P5 is typically ongoing" and routes production issues back_to_P3_P4 as "a new development cycle". Even the phase model reflow2 inherited did not assume termination. Found 2026-07-28 reviewing the original reflow workflows; reassessed the same day.
